articles.title: Ranking the Top 10 2027 NFL Free Agents Ahead of the 2026 Season-Opener
articles.summary: With the 2026 NFL regular season set to kick off on Wednesday, the 2027 offseason may feel like a distant event. After all, most teams are focused on chasing a championship, and Super Bowl LXI is still more than five months away.
articles.body:
With the 2026 NFL regular season set to kick off on Wednesday, the 2027 offseason may feel like a distant event. After all, most teams are focused on chasing a championship, and Super Bowl LXI is still more than five months away.

You can bet, though, that teams looking to build long-term already have one eye on next year's free-agent class. Some very good players are set to be available when next year's market opens on March 11, and teams are already trying to decide who to target, who to lock up, and how pricey contracts may get.

Here, we'll take our own dive into the 2027 free-agent class and rank the top 10 players based on past production, player upside, age, positional value, and player health.

We'll also make contract projections based on recent signings, projected positional demand, and the rest of the upcoming free-agent landscape.

For Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch, a lot will hinge on his ability to get and stay healthy in 2026. He'll begin the 2026 season on the physically unable to perform list while continuing to recover from a torn Achilles.

However, the Lions do believe that Branch and fellow safety Kerby Joseph (knee) will be available early in the year.

"They're both here, they're rehabbing, they're working hard, just can't offer a timeline but yeah, the hope is to have both of them back soon," GM Brad Holmes said, per ESPN's Eric Woodyard .

If Branch is back to pre-injury form this season, the 24-year-old should earn a contract that approaches the top of the market—which Kyle Hamilton currently tops with an average salary of $25.1 million. In 43 career games, Branch has logged seven interceptions, 4.5 sacks, and three forced fumbles while allowing an opposing passer rating of only 80.4 in coverage.

Projected Contract Value: Four Years, $80 Million

9. Joey Porter Jr., CB, Pittsburgh Steelers

Though he hasn't quite cracked the ranks of the elite, Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has been in the top tier since entering the league as a 2023 second-round pick.

Porter has appeared in 47 games with 41 starts and has allowed an opposing passer rating of only 71.2 in coverage. This past season, the 26-year-old was graded 36th overall among qualifying corners by Pro Football Focus .

The Steelers and Porter appear to be in a contract standoff that could potentially lead to a trade or a holdout during the regular season, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

"Sources say the Steelers' lack of a formal offer for weeks sent the clear message to Porter that they would like him to play out the final year of his rookie contract," Fowler wrote.

Porter's next contract will probably come in a bit below the top of the market. If he doesn't sign until next offseason and has a career year in 2026, though, that could change.

Projected Contract Value: Three Years, $74 Million

Like Branch, Lions tight end Sam LaPorta carries some injury concerns heading into 2026. He suffered a season-ending back injury last year and dealt with a hip injury during training camp.

However, LaPorta has returned to practice and appears on track to start in Week 1. He and Branch both remain in Detroit's long-term plans, too.

"There's a couple factors that we've still got to sort through. But in terms of us wanting those guys around? Absolutely," GM Brad Holmes said, per Richard Silva of The Detroit News. "Hopefully, we can get that done."

When healthy, LaPorta has been one of the league's best pass-catching tight ends, and he should be paid accordingly. The 25-year-old has recorded 2,104 yards and 20 touchdowns in 42 regular-season games.

Projected Contract Value: Four Years, $72 Million

With Jared Verse immediately becoming a star, Byron Young has largely been viewed as the Los Angeles Rams' other pass-rusher over the last couple of seasons. That's not going to change in 2026, as the Rams have replaced Verse with reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett.

However, Young is a terrific edge player who can pressure quarterbacks, meet ball-carriers in the backfield, and maintain gap integrity on the perimeter. He led the Rams with 12.0 sacks in 2025 but has regularly flashed as an all-around player.

In three seasons, the 2023 third-round pick has recorded 205 tackles, 27.5 sacks, 32 tackles for loss, and four forced fumbles. He made his first Pro Bowl in 2025.

The one potential concern with Young is the fact that he entered the NFL as an older prospect and will turn 29 in March. He should have many good years in front of him, but he may garner shorter contract offers than some of his peers.

Projected Contract Value: Three Years, $90 Million

6. Tuli Tuipulotu, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

Top-tier edge-rushers always command a high market value, and Tuli Tuipulotu is on the cusp of proving that he is one of them. The 2023 second-round pick out of USC has steadily grown during his three seasons with the Los Angeles Chargers.

Following an 8.5-sack breakout campaign in 2024, Tuipulotu graduated to Pro Bowl status in 2025. He finished last year's campaign with 13 sacks, 20 tackles for loss, and 32 quarterback pressures.

Tuipulotu is unlikely to approach market leaders like Maxx Crosby, T.J. Watt, and Myles Garrett in terms of contract value. However, he could get a deal that comes closer to the top of the market than its mid-level.

Having just turned 24 on September 3, Tuipulotu is only now entering his playing prime. He could also hit the open market coming off of back-to-back double-digit-sack campaigns, which would make him very attractive in free agency.

Projected Contract Value: Four Years, $105 Million

George Pickens is set to play a second season with the Dallas Cowboys on the franchise tag. If he's able to replicate last year's production, he'll likely move even further up the free-agent rankings.

Pickens shared targets with an elite receiver in CeeDee Lamb and still managed to rack up 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns in 2025. He's also still only 25 years old.

However, Pickens will need to show that he can consistently produce at a Pro Bowl level to earn a top-of-the-market deal. His production fluctuated during his three seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and Pittsburgh was willing to trade him for third- and fifth-round picks last offseason.

Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin also questioned Pickens' ability to be a leader following the trade, which probably won't be forgotten by some team decision-makers.

If Pickens has another Pro Bowl season while continuing to repair his locker-room reputation, he should be able to match recent receiver deals—like Drake London's four-year, $141.1 million extension—on the open market.

Projected Contract Value: Four Years, $142 Million

4. Quenton Nelson, G, Indianapolis Colts

Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson has been going strong since he was drafted sixth overall in 2018. He's been named to the Pro Bowl in all eight of his seasons and has been a first-team All-Pro three times.

While Nelson has already put together a career that might earn him Hall of Fame consideration, he's still only 30, is playing at an extremely high level, and remains remarkably durable.

Nelson has started all 17 games in each of the past four seasons. In 2025, Pro Football Focus graded him 4th overall among all qualifying guards.

It's difficult to envision Nelson playing for a different franchise with several quality years likely to come. However, price could become a significant factor for the Colts. Nelson is likely seeking a contract that will top every non-tackle offensive line deal in the NFL.

Tyler Linderbaum currently leads the interior-lineman market with a $27 million annual value.

Projected Contract Value: Four Years, $109 Million

Aaron Donald is back and is ready to resume his role as the Rams' star defensive tackle. However, he won't be the only top-tier interior defender in Los Angeles' lineup this season.

Kobie Turner hasn't made fans forget about Donald over the last couple of years, but he's done a very admirable job of filling the future Hall of Famer's shoes. The 27-year-old has been extremely productive while also proving to be incredibly durable.

Turner has appeared in all 51 regular-season games since he was drafted and has recorded 167 tackles, 24 sacks, 27 tackles for loss, and 62 quarterback pressures. Pro Football Focus graded him sixth overall among defensive tackles in 2025.

Elite interior defenders are coveted in today's NFL, and Turner will have multiple interested suitors if he reaches free agency. He may not top Jalen Carter as the league's highest-paid defensive tackle, but his next contract should rival those of recently-extended DTs like Quinnen Williams and Jeffery Simmons.

Projected Contract Value: Four Years, $141.5 Million

2. Baker Mayfield, QB, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Quarterback Baker Mayfield is betting on himself once again. The 2018 first overall pick wanted to sign an extension with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before the start of training camp. That didn't happen, and so the former Heisman winner will play out the final year of his deal.

"So, we'll just have to see how it plays out," GM Jason Licht said, per ESPN's Jenna Laine . "I'll never close the door on anything in the short term, but right now, he's focused on football."

If Mayfield has another Pro Bowl-caliber season for Tampa, the Bucs will likely retain him—either with a new contract or via the franchise tag. In three seasons with the franchise, the 31-year-old has made two Pro Bowls, delivered two division titles, and has passed for 12,237 yards and 95 touchdowns.

Only Jared Goff has thrown more touchdown passes (101) over the last three seasons.

While Mayfield isn't quite an elite quarterback, he's the top signal-caller scheduled to be available in 2027. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler (h/t Laine ), Mayfield wants a contract comparable to those of Jordan Love, Trevor Lawrence, and Brock Purdy. Barring a major step backward on the field, he should get it.

Projected Contract Value: Four Years, $215 Million

Though he entered the league as a relatively unheralded fifth-round draft pick out of BYU, Puka Nacua has since established himself as one of the best offensive playmakers in the game.

The 25-year-old led the NFL in receptions last season with 129 and has racked up 4191 yards in just three seasons. Getting to play with reigning MVP Matthew Stafford has certainly helped Nacua's production, but he's still a top-tier wideout who is just entering his prime.

Nacua became extension-eligible this offseason and has certainly earned a second contract. Unlike some players, though, he hasn't considered holding out.

"It never crossed my mind that I don't want to be out there with those guys," Nacua said, per Greg Beacham of the Associated Press.

It'll be a surprise if Los Angeles allows Nacua to reach the market, especially with a transition to quarterback Ty Simpson coming at some point in the next few years. Whether he re-signs with the Rams or becomes an unrestricted free agent, though, Nacua should become the new highest-paid receiver in the NFL.

Projected Contract Value: Four Years, $170 Million

articles.title: B/R's 25 Best Fantasy Football Team Names of 2026
articles.summary: There are a number of steps to building a championship fantasy roster.
articles.body:
There are a number of steps to building a championship fantasy roster.

The first is preparation—the practice reps ahead of the biggest day on the fantasy calendar. The second is that biggest of days—draft day. While a good draft is critical though, it's only half the battle. There is roster management throughout the season. Navigating injuries. Hitting the waiver wire. Making trades.

If you want the prize, you have to put in the work.

But there's a final step—an incredibly important one. The last piece of the puzzle. The icing on the cake. The one thing that will push your fantasy squad over the top.

Your team has to have a good name. It is scientifically impossible to find glory without one.

Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was regarded as a risky fantasy investment by most in 2026—he was drafted well outside the top-12 fantasy quarterbacks after a disappointing end to his tenure with the Arizona Cardinals.

But at his best, Murray has been an elite fantasy option—he flirted with 4,000 passing yards, added over 800 yards on the ground and was the runner-up in fantasy points back in 2020 .

We have already seen Vikings head coach Kevin O' Connell work magic with another scrap-heap quarterback. If lightning strikes twice, Murray will win leagues.

George Kittle is equal parts awesome and infuriating for fantasy managers. Has been for years.

When he's healthy, Kittle is an elite fantasy option—in the past four years, he has finished as a top-three tight end in PPR points per game three times. But injuries are a fact of life with Kittle—he missed six games last year and is trying to work back from an Achilles tear suffered in the playoffs.

Those injuries knocked Kittle into low-end TE1 territory in 12-team fantasy leagues over the summer—a risky play that could return a hefty reward.

Plus, he's genuinely fun to root for and has glorious hair.

Breece Hall's fourth season with the New York Jets was his best—the 25-year-old surpassed 1,000 yards on the ground for the first time and topped 1,400 total yards on the way to an RB21 finish in PPR points.

Bigger and better things are expected of Hall in 2026, but there has already been an injury scare with the youngster—Hall suffered a groin injury in camp that cast doubt over his availability for Week 1.

However, Hall is expected to be ready for the opener against the Tennessee Titans, where he will try to stealthily make his way through holes in the front and ambush Titans defenders in the open field.

Inferno is the first part of Dante Alighieri's 14th-century narrative poem The Divine Comedy. In it, Dante is guided through the nine levels of Hell by the ancient Roman poet Virgil—beginning with Limbo.

That's where the Philadelphia Eagles hope their passing game won't be after trading A.J. Brown in the offseason—stuck in Limbo.

For that to be the case, DeVonta Smith will have to step up and show he can be Philly's new No. 1 wideout. The "Slim Reaper" would certainly appear to have what it takes to step into the role—he has eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards in three of the past four seasons, including in 2025.

The New York Giants are hoping to turn things around this year, and their young core of offensive skill-position players are the reason for much of that optimism. Wide receiver Malik Nabers is an important part of that core.

There are no insurances (get it?) that Nabers will be able to play in Week 1 after his 2025 season was ended by an ACL tear. But we saw the kind of damage Nabers can do two seasons ago—as a rookie Nabers caught 109 passes, topped 1,200 yards and finished sixth among receivers in PPR points.

At the conclusion of Revenge of the Sith , Anakin Skywalker tells Obi-Wan Kenobi that he underestimates his power before leaping toward him to deliver a fatal blow.

Skywalker then gets cut in half, because oops.

No one in the NFL is underestimating Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers anymore—as a rookie, Bowers broke the record for receiving yards by a rookie tight end—a record that had stood since 1961. He also set the high-water mark for catches by a rookie at any position.

Bowers' numbers were down in an injury-marred 2025 season, but fantasy managers are banking on a bounceback—he was the first player at his position drafted on average this summer.

Since 1979, Nickelodeon has been providing television programming that children enjoy and parents endure. There have been cartoons. Game shows. NFL broadcasts. And buckets and buckets of slime.

Houston Texans wideout Nico Collins hasn't been at it quite that long—if he had he'd be awfully old for a football player. But since 2021 Collins has been entertaining fans and making opposing defenses pull their hair out, surpassing 1,000 receiving yards in each of the past three seasons.

Fantasy managers have big expectations for Collins as the Texans' unquestioned No. 1 receiver—he was drafted in the second round on average as a top-10 fantasy option.

Are you a fan of decent (if unspectacular) bowls of Fettucine Alfredo? All the soup, salad and breadsticks you can eat?

Then you should absolutely have New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chis Olave on your roster.

Olave had the best season of his professional career in 2025, setting career highs in receptions (100), receiving yards (1,163) and touchdowns (9) on the way to finishing sixth in PPR points among wide receivers.

Now, with rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson sidelined indefinitely, Olave should see an endless basket of targets similar to last year's 156—fifth-most in the league.

Hopefully, the ball won't be covered in garlic butter.

With each passing year, it becomes harder and harder to believe that Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua was a fifth round pick.

As a rookie, Nacua set an NFL record for receptions by a first-year player with 105, piled up 1,575 total yards and finished fourth in PPR points among wideouts. After injuries hampered Nacua in 2024, he went that huge year one better in 2025—Nacua led the league in receptions and receiving yards per game, topped 1,800 total yards and finished with more PPR points than any player at his position.

I love the smell of Nacua in the morning. It smells like victory.

After an outstanding rookie season where he caught 82 passes, topped 1,100 yards and scored seven touchdowns on the way to a top-15 fantasy finish, Ladd McConkey of the Los Angeles Chargers suffered though a down 2025 where he caught just 66 passes and failed to hit 800 receiving yards.

However, in 2026 it's going to be on like McConkey Kong in Los Angeles.

With Keenan Allen and his team-high 122 targets a year ago now catching passes in Indianapolis, McConkey is a good bet to see 120 targets this year. If that's the case and McConkey can jump a few barrels and climb a few ladders, he'll save Pauline—and win fantasy managers championships.

Kyren Williams of the Los Angeles Rams is something of the Rodney Dangerfield of running backs—the man just can't get no respect.

In each of the past three seasons, Williams has posted at least 1,350 total yards. In each of the past three seasons, Williams has found the end zone at least 13 times. And in each of the past three seasons, Williams was a top-10 fantasy running back in PPR points.

However, after Blake Corun ate into Williams' workload over the second half of last season, his asking price in drafts over the summer dropped to RB15.

The lead back for one of the league's best offenses available in RB2 territory?

Sure, you'd expect a play on words involving Taylor Swift to somehow involve Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce.

You may not have heard, but they got married this offseason.

But when someone offers up a BP fastball, you just mash it over the fence.

Last year, Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor led the league with 323 carries and 18 touchdowns on the ground. He flirted with 2,000 total yards and finished the season fourth in PPR points among running backs.

There are similar expectations surrounding Taylor this season, and he should be a focal point of the Colts offense again this year.

Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs was the consensus first overall pick in fantasy football drafts this summer—and with good reason. Last year was the second consecutive season that Gibbs topped 1,800 total yards. Over that span he has a staggering 38 total touchdowns.

Gibbs was third in PPR points among running backs behind Bijan Robinson and Christian McCaffrey in 2025 after leading the position two years ago. And with David Montgomery now in Houston, Gibbs could be headed toward the heaviest workload of his career.

Gibbs could easily be headed toward Rick-rolling opponents on a weekly basis.

He's going to run around. But Gibbs won't desert you.

According to Merriam-Webster, je ne sais quoi is defined as, "something (such as an appealing quality) that cannot be adequately described or expressed."

That rather fits with Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley—at his best it can be difficult to adequately describe or express just how dangerous he is with a football in his hands.

That Barkley's 1,413 total yards last year was considered a "down" season shows how high the standard is with him. Over eight years with the Eagles and Giants, Barkley has topped 2,000 total yards and led the league in that category twice, including a 2024 campaign where he became the ninth back in NFL history to rush for over 2,000 yards.

Confession time—Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle was one of this analyst's favorite fantasy values in 2026. His average draft position was barely inside the top-20 at wideout. He has legitimate top-10 upside.

We have seen that upside in the past—he was eighth in PPR points with the Dolphins in 2022. We have seen Waddle catch 100 passes. And lead the NFL in yards per reception.

Waddle is going to emerge as Bo Nix's favorite target in the Mile High City. He could easily have the best season of his professional career.

And Waddle is going to strut down the runway with such panache that it would make Derek Zoolander blush.

This one might be a little mean—but that doesn't mean it isn't funny.

Christin McCaffrey of the San Francisco 49ers was fantasy football's No. 1 running back last year, picking up 2,126 total yards and scoring 17 times.

McCaffrey's big season came after a career-high 413 touches—and the history of players in the season following a 2,000-yard campaign is…not great.

That also marked the third time McCaffrey has gained 2,000 yards in a season. After each of the last two, he missed 13 games.

McCaffrey is also a 30-year-old back—well past the age where players at his position generally start to decline.

Come on. You had to know that there was going to be toilet humor at some point in this hit.

Detroit Lions tight end Sam Laporta burst into fantasy prominence as a rookie, turning 120 targets into 86 receptions, 889 yards, 10 touchdowns and the top spot in PPR points among tight ends.

The last two years haven't been as productive, largely due to injuries—LaPorta's numbers dropped across the board in 2024, and while LaPorta was seventh in PPR points per game among tight ends a back injury cost him almost half the season.

Still, LaPorta has shown elite upside on a potent offense.

"Never meant to make your daughter cry, I apologized a trillion times."

Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba made more than a few fantasy opponents OutKasts from the playoffs last year—a third-round pick on average, Smith-Njigba erupted for an NFL-high 1,793 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns on the way to winning Offensive Player of the Year honors. Only Puka Nacua of the Rams had more PPR points among wide receivers.

Smith-Njigba was targeted 163 times last year, and there's no reason to think that he won't be among the most productive players at his position in fantasy football once again in 2026.

"Knee deep in the hoopla. Sinking in your fight."

"Too many runaways. Eating up the night."

Guessing those lyrics went sailing over a lotta heads. My apologies. I'm old.

For the (hopefully) much smaller crowd who doesn't the reference at all, The "Griddy" is the preferred touchdown dance of Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson. Once regarded as arguably the best receiver in fantasy football, Jefferson fell from the first round of many drafts altogether this year after a "down" (by his standards) 2025 campaign.

That down season had a lot more to do with J.J. McCarthy being terrible at throwing a football than anything Jefferson did in 2025. No one is going to confuse Kyler Murray with Patrick Mahomes, but he's a big step in the right direction under center.

Jefferson will be doing significantly more dancing this year.

More than once over the history of the league, the NFL has been compared to gladiatorial combat—and its players to gladiators.

Well, if Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase lived in Ancient Rome, his name would be Catchimus Maximus.

Two years ago, Chase became the fifth wide receiver in the Super Bowl era to win the "Triple Crown" and lead the league in receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Last year Chase paced the NFL with a whopping 185 targets despite being without his bae Joe Burrow for most of the year.

There's a reason Chase was the first wideout drafted on average in 2026.

The best part about this fantasy team name is its versatility—and its accuracy.

By Week 3, we all feel like fantasy frauds. Goes with the game. I do 11 minutes after each draft.

This name could apply to New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, who was a league-winner for fantasy managers in his second professional season. An 11th-round pick on average, Maye finished fourth in the league in passing yards, third in passing scores, fourth among quarterbacks with 450 rushing yards and third at the position in fantasy points.

Or it could apply to Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London, who ranked eighth in PPR points per game among receivers last year and fourth in PPR points at the position the year before.

If both are on your roster, it's kismet. Fate.

"I'll just toss that ham in the frying pan."

"Like Spam, get done when I come and slam."

About the only lyrics from that song I can include here without getting fired.

Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane had a coming-out party in 2025—1,350 rushing yards, an NFL-high 5.7 yards per carry, over 1,800 total yards and a fifth-place finish in PPR points at his position.

The good news for Achane managers is that his ceiling could be even higher than that—he's just about the only weapon the woeful Dolphins have on offense.

The bad news is that Miami's opponents know that too—and the 5'9", 195-pounder isn't exactly built for a 400-touch workload.

This one should amuse everyone except LSU fans—and given the madness going on in Baton Rouge right now, outrage from that crowd would seem, um, misplaced.

Frankly, it's absurd that Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels would be so outraged about the Tigers giving his number to another player that he sent the school a cease-and-desist letter—regardless of what he was told about the sanctity of No. 5.

Yes, he won the Heisman. But he didn't win a championship—and there are only 100 numbers to go around.

If you really want to see this name through, email your opponent an injunction every week that forbids them from winning because it will hurt your feelings.

Come on, who doesn't love a play on words involving a nearly-defunct store that sold overpriced toasters, every scent of candle imaginable and expensive sheet sets that weren't all that comfortable?

There's nothing funny about how Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson has played the past couple of seasons. After almost 1,900 total yards and 15 touchdowns in 2024, Robinson was even better in some respects in 2025, pacing the NFL with a whopping 2,298 total yards and finishing as a top-five running back for the second consecutive campaign.

Once Robinson wins you a championship (again) you can hop online (BB&B still exists there) and buy yourself a nice waffle maker.

Given his age and career workload, the odds are stacked against Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry having another big season. Father Time, as they say, is undefeated.

Or at least he was. King Henry fears no man. He will stiff-arm Father Time into an alternate reality. Father Time is so afraid of Henry he pays him protection money.

When Derrick Henry does push-ups, he pushes the earth down instead of pushing himself up.

If you ask Derrick Henry what time it is, he always says, "Two seconds till." After you ask, "Two seconds to what?" he stiff-arms you in the face.

Derrick Henry does not own a stove, oven or microwave, because revenge is a dish best served cold.

articles.title: Bad Bunny Wins Emmy for NFL Super Bowl 60 Halftime Show After 9 Nominations
articles.summary: Bad Bunny dazzled audiences during his halftime show of this past season's Super Bowl LX between the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks, and he took home plenty of hardware as a result.
articles.body:
Bad Bunny dazzled audiences during his halftime show of this past season's Super Bowl LX between the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks, and he took home plenty of hardware as a result.

Jazz Tangcay of Variety reported Saturday that Bad Bunny won his first Emmy for the performance in the category of outstanding variety special (live).

The halftime show ended up winning in seven different categories, including music direction, choreography, sound mixing, lighting design, technical direction/camerawork and directing. Jay-Z also won an Emmy as the executive producer.

Former NFL DB, College All-American Dies at 40

Jay-Z's Roc Nation has helped choose the Super Bowl halftime performer since partnering with the NFL in 2020.

According to Paul Grein of Billboard , the Bad Bunny show became the second Super Bowl halftime performance to win the top program Emmy. The first came four years ago when the show starring a collection of superstars in Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Kendrick Lamar, Mary J. Blige and 50 Cent won.

Bad Bunny's show also surpassed that 2022 one as the most-awarded Super Bowl halftime performance in Emmy history. The one featuring Dr. Dre and Co. won three.

It was not the first time Bad Bunny took the Super Bowl stage, as he also was a guest performer in 2020 when he joined Jennifer Lopez and Shakira.

Yet he was center stage during this past Super Bowl and put on a memorable performance that included appearances by Lady Gaga, Cardi B, Ricky Martin, Pedro Pascal, Karol G and many more.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Sleeper RBs to Target in Updated Flex Rankings
articles.summary: Some might call them procrastinators, while others know they're strategy geniuses. We're talking, of course, about fantasy managers who hold their drafts on or after Labor Day weekend.
articles.body: Some might call them procrastinators, while others know they're strategy geniuses. We're talking, of course, about fantasy managers who hold their drafts on or after Labor Day weekend. There are far more pitfalls to having your draft too early than too late. Players might not make the 53-man roster, get injured in preseason games or even be placed on the commissioner's exempt list for an indeterminate amount of time. If you're about to select your team, here are updated flex rankings . Below you'll find analysis of sleeper running backs specifically who can make sure you have a bench that can carry you to the championship. Rankings via FantasyPros and assume PPR scoring. FantasyPros' definition of sleepers is players who "have a strong chance to exceed expectations to become surprise difference-makers for fantasy managers." Kaleb Johnson, RB, Green Bay Packers A couple weeks ago, when it was first announced that Packers starter Josh Jacobs would be on the commissioner's exempt list for an indeterminate amount of time, savvy fantasy managers made sure to draft MarShawn Lloyd, who looks to get the bulk of the carries in the Packers backfield as long as Jacobs is unable to play. Lloyd is no longer a sleeper—but Kaleb Johnson is, and he's worth adding to your bench in case Lloyd is injured or the Packers go to more of a committee approach. Remember that Lloyd has still only played 10 regular season snaps as he has dealt with being injured. The Packers acquired Johnson from the Pittsburgh Steelers in exchange for a sixth-round pick. The 2025 third-round pick led the Big Ten in rushing yards in 2024, but he was never able to translate that production to an NFL field with the Steelers. Johnson has an average draft position (ADP) of RB62. But that means that in a 12-person league, he's likely to be on someone's bench, so draft him now while you can. How you value Brian Robinson Jr. in your draft depends on what you thought about Tyler Allgeier's role as essentially a handcuff option for Bijan Robinson in Atlanta the last three seasons. Robinson Jr. plays a similar game to Allgeier's, with high-upside red-zone potential. Robinson looks to be a good handcuff option for, uh, Robinson. Bijan Robinson enters the 2026 season as an elite fantasy running back, going in the top of the first round in most drafts. However, Atlanta often used Tyler Allgeier last year as the second part of a two-headed running back pairing, rushing 143 times for 8 touchdowns in 2025 as the backup. Allgeier's physical running style made him an ideal choice near the goal line and red zone, with the Falcons going with an almost 50/50 split for carries between the two in 2025. However, after Allgeier signed with the Arizona Cardinals in free agency this year, the Falcons swooped in and signed Brian Robinson Jr. to pair with Bijan Robinson for 2026. Brian Robinson Jr.'s physical running style lends itself to a similar pairing with Bijan, and with the Falcons going into the season with only the two running backs on the active roster, it seems likely Robinson Jr. will see goal-line touches that may siphon some away from Bijan Robinson. Add in the fact that Atlanta continues to look for answers at the quarterback position, with the decision between Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa coming down to the wire, and leaning on the running game seems like an obvious answer for new head coach Kevin Stefanski. Pairing the Robinsons (or at least picking up Robinson Jr. as a touchdown vulture) feels like a good bet before the season starts. Kaelon Black, RB, San Francisco 49ers If there are two things you can count on with the San Francisco 49ers, they are a heavy emphasis on the running game and the knowledge that injuries are coming. (We could make an electrical substation joke, but that seems too easy.) Christian McCaffrey is the no-doubt RB1 for the 49ers, but despite his continued prolific stats, he turned 30 years old in June and has an extensive injury history. The 49ers are also already feeling the injury bug at other skill positions on the roster, with wide receivers Ricky Pearsall and Christian Kirk on injured reserve (with Kirk designated for return this season), Mike Evans and rookie De'Zhuan Stribling questionable at the start of the season, and tight end George Kittle recovering from a torn achilles tendon last year. Although Black is a third-round rookie, he has reportedly taken over the backup role for the 49ers, excelling in training camp and the preseason. Expect head coach Kyle Shanahan to lean on the running game early on in the season and find ways to get Black into games to spell McCaffrey. Should McCaffrey miss any time, Black's workload is sure to receive a massive jump. It may be worth picking up Black as a handcuff to McCaffrey or stashing him on your bench in case the substation strikes again.

articles.title: How Many Hours It Took to Build Broncos' New $175M 'State-of-the-Art' Facility Revealed
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos' new "state-of-the-art" facility took 750,000 total man hours to complete, per ESPN's Jeff Legwold, and has certainly caught the attention of the team's players.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos' new "state-of-the-art" facility took 750,000 total man hours to complete, per ESPN's Jeff Legwold , and has certainly caught the attention of the team's players.

"I said it last year when they were still building it, I say 'look at it, just look at it,'" running back J.K. Dobbins said. "How are you going to be a player and you see the coaches, the team, the people and where we go every day and not want to be here? Nobody else has one of these."

Defensive tackle D.J. Jones said it is a "10 out of 10," while cornerback Pat Surtain II said, "Everything is state-of-the-art. When I first got in ... I was looking at it and I was like, 'Wow.' I was in awe."

Buzz: Baker Frustrated with Bucs Talks 😠

Legwold noted the complex cost $175 million and was done in an effort to get the majority of the team's employees under one roof.

"Every day I walk the building, I see different parts for the first time post-construction and I think it's amazing," Broncos president Damani Leech said. "It's a testament to ownership, to Greg and Carrie [Penner], the investment they've made into football ... but also our business to ... create culture, to design a building with football in mind.

"I love coming to work every day, and I think everybody else does, too."

The facility is 240,000 square feet and 30 percent larger than the previous one.

It has three floors, the first of which is for the players and includes a locker room with 102 lockers, an equipment room, a training room, a weight room, a cafeteria, a lap pool and a hallway to the indoor practice facility, which stands in stark contrast to the last one where players had to leave the main building and go outside into the Colorado winter air to get to the indoor practice building.

The second floor features offices for head coach Sean Payton and general manager George Paton, as well as working space for the coaches, personnel and scouting staffs.

What's more, the third floor includes an employee fitness center and a golf simulator.

With the new facility now complete, the team can turn its attention to its season opener against the rival Kansas City Chiefs on Sept. 14 at 8:15 p.m. ET.

articles.title: New Seahawks Rumors on JSN, Jadarian Price, Rashid Shaheed and Fantasy Implications vs. Patriots
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks are the reigning Super Bowl champions, but their offense could feature even more production from different players during the 2026 campaign.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks are the reigning Super Bowl champions, but their offense could feature even more production from different players during the 2026 campaign.

"Seattle players are ecstatic about this new offense under OC Brian Fleury," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Sunday on SportsCenter . "It will have shades of the 49ers with the motions and the shifts. You're going to see a lot of two tight ends; AJ Barner, Elijah Arroyo playing together on the field a lot, most likely on Wednesday night creating holes for the run game.

"Watch for Rashid Shaheed, the speedster that came over via trade last year, wasn't really acclimated to the offense because he came in midseason, I'm told he's had a killer offseason. So, Jaxon Smith-Njigba's going to get a ton of targets; last year he had like nearly 40 percent of the targets, you'll see Shaheed getting some of those. And then Jadarian Price, the rookie, he'll be a factor Wednesday night, but the Seahawks do want to have two-to-three backs per game that they're utilizing. They don't want to overload him too early."

Buzz: Baker Frustrated with Bucs Talks 😠

Multiple parts of Fowler's report are sure to catch the eye of fantasy football managers ahead of Seattle's season opener and Super Bowl rematch against the New England Patriots on Wednesday.

And those with Smith-Njigba on their teams may not love it.

While the Ohio State product will surely remain on the short list of the best wide receivers in the league, Shaheed cutting into his overall targets could reduce his overall fantasy production. Those 163 targets last season helped him finish with 119 catches for an NFL-best 1,793 yards and 10 touchdowns.

Smith-Njigba was fantasy gold nearly every week last season at 105.5 receiving yards per game, and the reigning Offensive Player of the Year should still be an early draft pick ahead of the matchup with the Patriots.

He just might not be quite as statistically dominant, although that will increase Shaheed's value as a potential late-round steal in fantasy drafts.

Shaheed is best known for his speed, and Smith-Njigba is sure to draw double teams on a weekly basis. That should open up one-on-one opportunities for the secondary option, and all he will have to do is take advantage of one or two deep routes per game to be quite valuable in fantasy.

As for Price, he still brings plenty of upside over the course of the long season even if he may not be the correct play in daily fantasy for the game against New England if Seattle is going to ease him in with "two-to-three backs per game."

The Seahawks used a first-round pick on the Notre Dame running back and watched Kenneth Walker III join the Kansas City Chiefs. They are going to feature him throughout the season, and it would be anything but a surprise if he surpasses 1,000 yards on the ground as the top back.

But perhaps fantasy managers should temper their immediate expectations for the first game against New England as Price becomes adjusted to the NFL level.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald Ahead of Rams vs. 49ers amid Injury, Return
articles.summary: Despite some injury concerns for Myles Garrett and rust to work off for Aaron Donald, the pair of Los Angeles Rams stars reportedly could be on track to join forces along the defensive line for Thursday's season opener against the San Francisco 49ers.
articles.body:
Despite some injury concerns for Myles Garrett and rust to work off for Aaron Donald, the pair of Los Angeles Rams stars reportedly could be on track to join forces along the defensive line for Thursday's season opener against the San Francisco 49ers.

"Myles Garrett had a bit of a knee issue, really didn't do much at all throughout camp," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Sunday on SportsCenter . "They acquired him in June, brought him in. He hasn't been on the field a ton, but they're not really worried. They know he can roll out of bed and get sacks. He's been ramping up slowly but surely, lifting a lot of weights, now he's on the practice field. I'm hearing he should be good as well.

"The big question mark is Aaron Donald because they just acquired him, signed him last week. His training and all the workouts he did for the team have gone great. Looks like himself, but you know he's 35 years old; they want to make sure they ramp him up the right way. He made the trip, he might as well try to play, could be a pitch-count situation if he is out there."

There is far more certainty in Fowler's report when it comes to Garrett, which shouldn't be surprising.

After all, Donald hasn't played since the 2023 campaign and officially decided to come out of retirement less than two weeks before the season opener. It is unrealistic to expect him to be as dominant as he was at his peak, especially early in the season as he is working back into form.

Still, even 70 percent or so of what Donald was on a limited amount of plays would dramatically raise the ceiling for the Rams considering he is one of the best defensive tackles in league history with a resume that includes a Super Bowl title, three Defensive Player of the Year awards and six seasons with double-digit sacks.

As for Garrett, Fowler's report made it seem like the Rams aren't particularly concerned about his overall effectiveness in games despite the knee issue.

And that is welcome news for the rest of the defensive line as well considering the reigning Defensive Player of the Year is sure to draw double teams even when he is on the field with Donald.

That should open up blitzing lanes for everyone else and make Los Angeles even more of a nightmare to deal with for opposing offensive lines.

Garrett set the NFL single-season record with 23 sacks last season for the Cleveland Browns and is coming off his eighth consecutive year with double-digit sacks. He is nearly impossible to block and figures to have a chance at his first Super Bowl ring this season.

That journey to the Super Bowl starts with a season opener that carries plenty of implications against the NFC West rival 49ers.

The Rams, 49ers and Seattle Seahawks all made the playoffs last season with the latter winning the Super Bowl. They could all be among the best teams in the league again in 2026, so head-to-head tiebreakers could make the difference in the division standings.

articles.title: 2027 NFL Draft: 5 Prospects to watch in Ole Miss vs. Louisville
articles.summary: We have our eyes on several players in the Ole Miss' matchup with Louisville.
articles.body:
College football is back in our lives. Whether you are a fan of it or not, the Browns and their front office are going to be paying very close attention to a lot of players in the upcoming class. The 2027 NFL Draft is working up to be one of the better classes in recent memory.

One way to stay as caught up as the Browns will be is to follow our prospect previews starting now. We'll focus heavily on prospects who fit the team's projected needs in the 2027 NFL Draft. We are going to be looking at five players from the Ole Miss -Louisville matchup.

The game may not be very close, but the talent within the game is going to be interesting to see unfold in 2026, starting in Week 1. Here are the five players we are looking at from the game.

One of my favorite quarterbacks coming out of the summer was Trinidad Chambliss. Is he undersized? Yes. Is he a bit of a manic type out of the backfield? Also yes, but that is why I love him. He refuses to say die in the best ways possible, where he extends plays when pressured, and it allows him to find his receivers when the defense is forced to extend coverage. Louisville has a great defense; it will be a good test for him, and it is another national spotlight for him to shine under.

I had a first-round grade on Clev Lubin coming out of the summer. The motor is high, the hands are strong, and it allows him to knock around these NFL-sized offensive tackles in the ACC. Against Ole Miss, he will go against a tough offensive line, and the quarterback we just highlighted can extend plays. Lubin has the ability to contain Chambliss, and if he can, it will be a game-altering effort from him.

Suntarine Perkins is a unique study and hard to project in terms of his role in the NFL. He could be an edge but is a bit undersized, or he could be a linebacker but struggles with his movement ability at times. Despite that, he is still very much a problem in college football for now. Against a new Louisville quarterback, Perkins could prove to be someone who shifts the game one way or another.

Tre Richardson is an explosive receiver who has worked his way up from JUCO to the ACC now, and he deserves to have some shine. He is a receiver who can take the lid off a defense and score anytime he touches the ball. Look for Louisville to take advantage of the Rebels' cornerbacks and try to beat them with their speed, with Richardson leading the way.

My RB2 coming out of summer scouting is the dynamic Kewan Lacy. He is patient at the line of scrimmage, showcases explosiveness when hitting the second level, and he can handle a larger workload. Against Louisville and their talented defensive front, it will be a tough first test of the season, but it is one he should pass. Look for Lacy to flash some pass blocking as well to help out his quarterback against the dominant edge-rushing duo of the Cardinals.

articles.title: Browns fans have good reason to be NFL's least optimistic fanbase per The Athletic
articles.summary: This fan poll result is, unfortunately, entirely justified.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are coming into the 2026 NFL season likely to be one of the worst teams in the league. It would be a shocker if they made the playoffs, or even just had close to a .500 winning percentage.

This team just, simply put, isn't good enough right now. Looking into the future, there are plenty of question marks surrounding this team as well. So, for the loyal Browns fans who've stuck through thick and thin, how optimistic should they be?

According to Adam Coleman of The Athleti c, a poll conducted among fans of all NFL teams, the Browns fanbase was overwhelmingly the least optimistic in the league. Unfortunately, they have good reason to have such little optimism.

Browns are least optimistic fan base in NFL for good reason

Coleman shared that Browns fans handed out a brutal 2.7 percent optimism score, by far the lowest in the NFL. In 31st place, second-worst in the league, was the Miami Dolphins ' fanbase, which at least had 11.1 percent optimism.

There is only one team's fanbase where at least 90% of the fanbase is not optimistic, and it's the Browns. This is warranted for a few reasons.

Trading Myles Garrett is certainly a huge blow, especially after he just set the sack record. Losing Jim Schartz also doesn't help.

Looking to the offensive side of the ball, Deshaun Watson being named the starting quarterback is such a major letdown for Browns fans that there is very little to be excited about to start the season.

Watson isn't their QB of the future. Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel, and Taylen Green probably aren't either, but they are at least more exciting options who have somewhat of a chance of being a decent QB in the NFL.

It should not be a surprise that Browns fans are the least optimistic in the NFL. But there are still some things worth getting excited about.

Quinshon Judkins, Harold Fannin Jr., Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion are a nice set of weapons on offense. If they can find a franchise QB and improve the offensive line further, this offense might actually be decent.

Defensively, they have Jared Verse, Emmanuel McNeill-Warren, Tyson Campbell, Mason Graham, and Carson Schwesinger as key pieces who should be around for a while. Plus, Denzel Ward is still in Cleveland and just signed a two-year extension.

With two first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft, there is a path towards success in the not-so-distant future for the Browns. The issue, however, is that the 2026 season is looking like it's going to be a brutal one.

Should Browns fans be the least optimistic in the NFL? Probably. But there is still some reason to have hope for the future; it's just not something that will materialize in 2026. Come back in a year, and things will, hopefully for Browns fans, feel a lot better.

articles.title: 2026 Fantasy Football 4-Round Mock Draft with Notable Picks
articles.summary: Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season has arrived.
articles.body:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season has arrived.

There will be actual games played on both Wednesday and Thursday night this week. And then, it'll be radio silence until everyone else gets rolling next Sunday and Monday.

Still, the wait is down to days and will soon shift to hours, then minutes, then seconds—and then boom, the opening kick gets booted, and everyone starts playing for real.

Fantasy football managers should be in fine-tuning mode with their draft plans, then, so let's help with the strategic refinement by running through a simulated four-round, 12-team PPR mock and highlighting notable picks in every round.

While there's nothing outlandish on the board here, there are a few notable things to spotlight.

First is the amount of trust being placed in McCaffrey as the fourth overall pick. He is obviously talented enough to live up to that billing—he ranked second among non-quarterbacks in fantasy points last season—but his worry list is not a short one. The red flags almost raise themselves for a 30-year-old back with a long injury history who's coming off of a 450-touch season.

The other interesting wrinkle is St. Brown landing ahead of Smith-Njigba. St. Brown is one of the safest options in fantasy, but he also has a lot more competition for targets than JSN, who just turned 163 targets into 119 receptions for 1,793 yards and 10 touchdowns last season.

Nothing really stands out about the receivers taken here, save perhaps for the confidence expressed in Nabers. He could be an awesome value as the 20th player taken, but he has often landed a little later to account for possible turbulence upon his return from a torn ACL and meniscus.

As for running backs, this seems a touch late on Hampton and a little early for Williams.

Hampton could be a fantasy monster with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel now at the controls. Williams, meanwhile, could face increasing competition for field time from Blake Corum, and if things shift more toward the latter, the former will have trouble living up to a second-round cost.

This is—as it should be—the first round not exclusively populated with running backs and receivers. Deviations are always notable, so let's focus on the quarterbacks and tight ends.

Fantasy analysts routinely advise managers to wait on quarterbacks, so they might label a third-round cost on any as too rich. If anyone is worth it, though, it's Allen. And the idea of taking him ahead of a long wait between picks is a fun one. It's harder to get behind third-round costs for Jackson and Maye, who don't carry the same guaranteed-greatness security.

As for the tight ends, this feels right for both McBride and Bowers. Folks will disagree on the order, but when they're so tightly bunched, it's just a matter of preference. And this just happens to align with our particular preference.

The mock drafters did well enough in the first three rounds that there aren't any major bargains here. That said, the price tag on Williams looks pretty great. He's a high-volume back in a high-volume offense; he probably belongs in the middle of the third round, so he's a solid value near the top of the fourth.

Loveland feels right as a TE3 with an entire tier to himself. He doesn't have the track record needed to crack the elite ranks at the position, but his ceiling stretches higher than anyone behind him.

Daniels being the lone quarterback taken in this round feels...fine. It's not a move we would make, but if he's active as a rusher, he should be a high-end quarterback. This still seems a round or two too early, but the same applied to Jackson and Maye, so that could've inflated all of the non-Allen quarterbacks in this mock.

articles.title: Roger Goodell Signs New NFL Contract, Latest Details on Expiration Date Ahead of 2026 Season
articles.summary: NFL commissioner Roger Goodell will be holding on to his position through the end of the decade.
articles.body:
NFL commissioner Roger Goodell will be holding on to his position through the end of the decade.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , NFL teams were notified on Sunday that Goodell signed a new four-year contract extension through the 2030 season that will expire on March 31, 2031. Schefter added that New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, chairman of the Compensation Committee, sent a memorandum announcing the news.

"Throughout the negotiation process, the Committee worked closely with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure a deal that aligns Roger's compensation with the League's long-term interests and success," Kraft wrote. "To that end, the agreement is heavily performance based, with more than 95% of the total compensation tied to Roger's and the NFL's performance measured against various metrics and at the discretion of the Compensation Committee. We believe we are very fortunate to have Roger at the helm for the next four years."

Buzz: Baker Frustrated with Bucs Talks 😠

Schefter pointed out that the NFL's current collective bargaining agreement with the players also expires in March 2031, lining up with the end of Goodell's contract.

Per Jayna Bardahl and Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, this marks Goodell's fifth contract extension. His last extension was signed in 2023 and was set to expire in March 2027.

Goodell has been the commissioner of the NFL since 2006, the eighth person in league history to hold the position. He succeeded the late Paul Tagliabue, who held the position for 17 years. By the time Goodell's new contract expires, he will be nearly 72 years old and will have held the position for 24 years .

Throughout his tenure, Goodell has overseen a period of immense financial success in the NFL. Sportico's Eben Novy-Williams and Kurt Badenhausen reported that the league is on track to surpass $25 billion in revenue by 2027, fulfilling a goal Goodell set in 2010, when league revenue was around $8 billion. Last month, the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks were sold to a group led by the Khosla family for $9.612 billion, the highest purchase price ever for an NFL team.

Goodell has also helped the NFL grow globally, with the league set to play a record nine international games across seven countries during the 2026 season.

It's clear that the league is confident that Goodell can help it reach even greater heights through the remainder of his tenure at the helm.

articles.title: NFL commissioner Roger Goodell finalizes 4-year extension through 2030 season
articles.summary: Goodell's new contract will end on March 31, 2031; the NFL's current CBA will expire the same month.
articles.body:
Roger Goodell is sticking around. The NFL commissioner reached agreement on a four-year extension through the 2030 season, the league announced Sunday.

Teams were informed about the extension Sunday, with the compensation committee sharing a letter with full ownership. The committee is made up of NFL team owners John Mara (Giants), Shad Khan (Jaguars), Jimmy Haslam (Browns), Michael Bidwill (Cardinals), Greg Penner (Broncos) and chairman Robert Kraft (Patriots).

In the letter, the committee said it was "pleased to announce" the extension, and that the group had worked with "an independent third-party compensation consultant" throughout the negotiation process, via ESPN's Adam Schefter .

"To that end, the agreement is heavily performance based, with more than 95% of the total compensation tied to Roger's and the NFL's performance measured against various metrics and at the discretion of the Compensation Committee," the letter said, via Schefter. "We believe we are very fortunate to have Roger at the helm for the next four years."

Goodell's new contract will end March 31, 2031. Notably, March 2031 is also when the NFL's current collective bargaining agreement will expire.

After decades as an NFL executive, Goodell was hired as the sixth commissioner of the league just ahead of the 2006 season, succeeding Paul Tagliabue. In 20 years at the helm, he has overseen multiple major changes, including the creation of the NFL's player-conduct policy in 2007, the continued growth of the sport overseas and the league's slow-but-steady attempts to mitigate head injuries.

Only Pete Rozelle, who held the role for 30 seasons, has stayed in the position longer. Goodell is entering his 21st season.

Though fans are not known to love him — Goodell gets booed on nearly every stage he enters — team owners clearly embrace him and the growth he has helped oversee, with league revenue ballooning to $14.5 billion this past season, via Sportico .

At the time that this current deal expires, Goodell will have just celebrated his 72nd birthday.

In the meantime, the commissioner is likely to pursue a few projects. Goodell has continued to push the idea of adding an international NFL team , and the growth of flag football as a sport ahead of the 2028 Olympics. He will also have to deal with more controversial things, like the league's diversity policies (especially after no Black head coaches were hired in the most recent head-coaching cycle) and the Chicago Bears' exploration of a stadium in Indiana , which Goodell has helped with in the past .

Goodell, who has overseen negotiations for two NFL CBAs in his tenure, will need to use that experience ahead of the next round of negotiations in 2031. Given the unease around negotiations in MLB , and the increasing economic growth in the NFL, this next CBA may be particularly thorny.

articles.title: Commanders mailbag: Daronte Jones, David Blough, Adam Peters’ grand plan
articles.summary: We discuss your topics (some serious, some not) in this Washington Commanders mailbag
articles.body:
The NFL spends the entire summer building up to the regular season, with training camps and preseason games leading up to initial 53-man roster construction at the roster cut deadline.

Then you've got this relatively quiet week leading up to Labor Day, where nothing much outside a few mostly closed practices. Gone is the cutdown drama and all those practice video clips that are given too much stock.

There's a small dead period without roster moves or big news. We're in it right now.

Next week is officially Week 1 . In other words, go time.

That makes this little lull a perfect time to discuss your questions and comments about what the Commanders have and what comes next. I asked for conversation topics and we got plenty. Let's get right to them in this Commanders mailbag:

I like the mystery to the coordinator plans. And I love that it's hopefully going to be revealed in 3D Technicolor minimum 4K reality surprise the Iggles into getting embarrassed. And they need to reserve just enough surprises for Dallas.

How this happens? No idea, not that it can't happen, I just don't know how it plays out. But there's guys all over that D that should be able to add a few bumps to Hurts. — ComplainingIsAPayne

The Commanders have played up the mystery element when talking about what we've seen schematically to this point, which is exactly what they should do heading into the 2026 campaign.

We can point to Brian Flores and Mike Zimmer and others as Daronte Jones influences, but we're not sure exactly how that will look. We can anticipate an attacking scheme with exotic looks when the Commanders blitz heavily or not. I think it's fair to assume there will be plays where the pressure is the coverage and Washington tries to live in the offensive backfield.

Jones should use mystery to his advantage, and then play off the Week 1 game tape in Week 2. With the schemes being implemented and the talent available, the Commanders should be a fun watch.

Will this new offensive scheme commit to the run? Can the new defensive scheme stop the run?Last year the Bears created a blueprint to beat the Eagles which they did 24-15 — JayGrudenSucks

I was at that game covering the Bears at the time, and it was a dominant showing to be sure. If you can run like the Bears did that day, you're going to win a ton.

There's plenty we don't know about how Commanders coordinator David Blough will ultimately call plays, but Ben Johnson's influence is virtually guaranteed. That means a heavy reliance on the run game and playaction off of that.

I would expect Blough to run a ton if its effective, using it as the foundation for everything else the Commanders do. Here's a start difference between the Bears' roster assembly and what the Commanders did this offseason. Chicago gave eight-figure AAV deals to the entire interior offensive line. They invested heavily in Joe Thuney, Jonah Jackson and Drew Dalman.

The Commanders spent elsewhere, and are trying to get by inside with Nick Allegretti and Chris Paul, alongside Sam Cosmi on the right. Washington has a first-round right tackle and spent heavy on Laremy Tunsil, who's no longer available.

Blough will have to adjust to that and play to the offense's strength, which is at receiver and tight end.

Is Washington's strategy of turning over the roster 20-30% a year and signing veterans to one and two year deals going to become the way this team does business beyond just the first year or two of this front office?

Unlike New England which started where we were in 2024 with a rookie quarterback and a questionable roster, they have made the commitments to go out and sign free agents LONG TERM and garner some element of roster stability.

Washington has avoided giving out any contracts that signal a player is going to be here for more than say 2 years, and I have never really seen an NFL team in the free agency era do that and be successful. — Ghost Rider

I believe I've mentioned this before in the article comments but, for those unaware, I'm a huge salary-cap and roster construction nerd. Always have been.

General manager Adam Peters' current use of the salary cap – the Commanders are in a good space with it – follows the strategy of a team that A. has a franchise quarterback on a rookie deal who's eligible for an extension soon. and B. hasn't drafted well in the recent past.

GMs love to hand out contract extensions to homegrown players. It's a pat on the back for a smart draft pick and a reward for a player working well within an organizational culture. Problem is that the Commanders have no one to extend.

They invested in a young, presumably ascending free agent like Odafe Oweh (four years) and gave three year deals to Leo Chenal and Chig Okonkwo.

Everything they've done to this point is about preparing to absorb the Daniels extension and function well after that. You can generally keep the first year cap number of a massive deal low (thanks to a signing bonus), so Washington can afford to pay bigger salaries to free agents over the next few years. In the Patriots example, Drake Maye was in his second season, so they had three years to spend big on other positions.

The Commanders lost a year in 2025, and are in a slightly different boat.

Does the team increase its life insurance coverage for the players (and traveling fans) when playing in Philly? — via Eidolons

Visiting fans have to pay a premium for hit-by-battery coverage, but it's always worth it. Those guys love chucking AAs. But, buyer beware: Dressing up as Santa Claus automatically voids the emotional distress plan. Get booed at your own risk.

Is DQ's hat on correctly if he walks backwards? — DGOLD510

This was but one question in a list of awesomeness y'all should check out in the mailbag Feed post. And, to answer this question directly, yes. And I'd love to see it. Quinn supposedly wears the hat backwards to create a relaxed environment and to foster players being themselves. Stories have been written on it. Like, several, to my shock. As a fellow backwards hat guy, I dig it.

articles.title: A trend that shows why Aaron Donald should still dominate for the Rams
articles.summary: Defensive tackles age more gracefully than many other positions.
articles.body:
One of the biggest questions around the NFL pertaining to Aaron Donald's return to the Los Angeles Rams is about whether or not he can still be the same Aaron Donald he was during his original run, when he was the best defensive player in football.

It's still entirely possible that he's a massively impactful piece for the Rams' defense, but at the same time the odds are slim he's as good as he was then. Again, he was previously the best defensive player in football and has since spent two years away from the game.

But there is one thing that's certainly working in his favor: the position he plays.

This isn't a hard-and-fast rule by any means, but generally speaking interior defensive linemen, especially ones that already play at a high level, often age more gracefully than other players and positions.

In 2025, there were just two interior defensive lineman 35 years old or older who played an NFL game. That's relevant, of course, because that's how old Donald is now. One was 36-year-old Cameron Heyward, one of the best defensive tackles of his era, who started all 17 games for the Pittsburgh Steelers and earned his second second-team All-Pro honor , and sixth All-Pro nod overall.

Then there's John Jenkins, who's never been a star but has been as steady as they come at the position. With the Baltimore Ravens last season, Jenkins started 14 games and played in all 17, forced a pair of fumbles and tallied a 64.7 PFF grade, which was 45th among 134 qualified interior defensive linemen. No, that's not a perfect metric, but you get the gist.

Go back a season prior, to 2024. Heyward was a first-team All-Pro at 35 years old, Jenkins (also then 35) posted the second-best Approximate Value (a metric from Pro-Football-Reference) of his career, and Linval Joseph had a fine if not unspectacular year in Dallas.

Pro-Football-Reference also lists Calais Campbell as a nose tackle in 2024, and if you want a shining example of a lineman who is just as effective as they continue to age, that's your guy.

This is just a small sample of examples overall. You can dig back through recent NFL history and find plenty of guys who fit this bill. Damon "Snacks" Harrison was a sought-after piece up front for years as he continued to age. In 2018, Buffalo Bills legend Kyle Williams was a Pro Bowler at 35 years old. The Carolina Panthers got a year's worth of quality snaps from 35-year-old Hollis Thomas in 2009.

The reason this feels relevant is that we're not just cherry picking one successful guy out of 20 options for all these years. There aren't many who last to that age, but the ones who do aren't just serviceable, they're legitimate needle movers.

That brings us back to Donald. Clearly, there's some positive history on his side here in the sense that older defensive linemen still make a positive impact, historically speaking. There's also the fact that, to paraphrase Scott Steiner, he's a genetic freak and he's not normal. No disrespect to even a future Hall of Famer like Heyward, but Donald is on the short list of the greatest players to ever suit up.

He may not be at the peak of his powers when he takes the field, whether that's in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia or later on. But there are still plenty of good reasons to believe Aaron Donald is going to be a game wrecker in his return to the field.

articles.title: NFL signs Roger Goodell through 2030 season as serious issues over antitrust exemption and ongoing growth loom
articles.summary: Roger Goodell's four-year NFL contract extension could reach $300 million over four years, with 95% of his total compensation tied to performance.
articles.body: Roger Goodell will remain the commissioner of America's strongest and most popular professional sports league at least through March of 2031, following an NFL announcement that he has signed a contract extension. The league's Compensation Committee on Sunday notified the league's owners that it reached a four-season extension with Goodell. The deal will carry Goodell through the end of the 2030 season and expire just prior to the 2031 NFL Draft when he will be 71 years old. Terms of the new extension are not known and won't be announced as they are between an individual and a privately held company. But one industry compensation consultant source told OutKick that Goodell was expected to reach $300 million over the four-year term if he meets the top tier of his deal's incentive thresholds. Compensation Committee Chairman Robert Kraft, the New England Patriots owner and ally of Goodell, sent a memo to the rest of the league's 31 owners announcing the deal: "As members of the Compensation Committee, we’re pleased to announce that we have reached agreement with Roger to remain as Commissioner through the 2030 League Season, ending on March 31, 2031. "Throughout the negotiation process, the Committee worked closely with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure a deal that aligns Roger’s compensation with the League’s long-term interests and success. "To that end, the agreement is heavily performance based, with more than 95% of the total compensation tied to Roger’s and the NFL’s performance measured against various metrics and at the discretion of the Compensation Committee. "We believe we are very fortunate to have Roger at the helm for the next four years. If any of you has any questions, please reach out to any of us." The memo is from Kraft, New York Giants owner John Mara, Jacksonville Jaguars owner Shad Khan, Cleveland Browns owner Jimmy Haslam, Arizona Cardinals owner Michael Bidwill, and Denver Broncos owner Greg Penner – all of whom make up the committee. This is Goodell's fifth contract extension since he became commissioner in September 2006. At the end of this extension, Goodell will have served 24 years in his role. That would make him the second-longest serving commissioner in league history behind only Pete Rozelle who served 29 years and 10 months from 1960 to 1989. NFL COMMISSIONER ROGER GOODELL CONFIRMS LEAGUE WANTS MULTIPLE TEAMS BASED OUTSIDE THE US: 'NO DOUBT' The NFL's current collective bargaining agreement, which Goodell helped finalize in 2020, expires in March 2031, when Goodell's new extension will expire. Goodell's tenure has been defined by aggressive commercial growth, enormous media-rights agreements, games expanding to international markets, increased emphasis on player safety and labor peace after the 2011 lockout. The valuation of franchises under Goodell has skyrocketed with the Seattle Seahawks being the latest example in a sale worth $9.612 billion. Those past victories and the possibility of new television contract coming online around 2029 and perhaps expansion of the business model to include flag football, more international revenue and games, and perhaps even expansion, obviously gave Goodell confidence to tie his compensation to performance incentives. CONGRESS TARGETS NFL'S $110B BROADCAST MODEL AS JIM JORDAN REQUESTS GOODELL TESTIFY AT JUNE 10 HEARING Simply: If he continues to author significant growth, he'll benefit. And if he doesn't, which would be highly improbable given the NFL's history, then he won't. Goodell, by the way, has not been without controversy during his tenure. He has guided the league through controversies such as Spygate, Deflategate, an apparent rise in domestic-violence cases, concussion concerns, protests by players during the national anthem, lawsuits, and criticism that league discipline can be inconsistent. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Kraft recently outlined how the commissioner and, indeed, the entire league is facing enormous pressure from Congress and other government entities tied to its 65-year-old antitrust exemption. There are serious questions whether the league is abusing it to gouge fans and force games behind paywalled streaming services and Goodell was even recently invited to testify on the subject before Congress. He declined. But with his new term now secured, the question remains when, rather than if, he'll have to answer for the league's polices before fans and lawmakers. articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 Cheat Sheet and Mobile, Printable Rankings for Mock Drafts
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season is here, and with it will come a nearly unquantifiable number of fantasy leagues of various sizes and formats. With the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots set to kick off the regular season on Wednesday, the final fantasy draft window has arrived.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is here, and with it will come a nearly unquantifiable number of fantasy leagues of various sizes and formats. With the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots set to kick off the regular season on Wednesday, the final fantasy draft window has arrived.

Naturally, one draft guide won't fit all flavors of season-long fantasy formats. However, this handy and mobile-friendly cheat sheet might help. We'll provide our updated point-per-reception (PPR) rankings for each key position and identify a few potential sleepers here.

First, though, let's run through a quick two-round, 12-team mock draft.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, Seattle Seahawks

Christian McCaffrey, RB, San Francisco 49ers

Omarion Hampton, RB, Los Angeles Chargers

Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff gets to work with one of the league's most dangerous collections of pass-catchers. Naturally, he's widely viewed as a surefire starter in fantasy, right?

Actually, he's regularly available late in drafts and carries an average draft position (ADP) of only 128. He finished last season as QB8 and could have a similar or even better finish under new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing.

And regardless of how much Petzing can or cannot boost the offense, Goff will still be tossing the ball to Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, and Jameson Williams.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

TreVeyon Henderson, New England Patriots

Rhamondre Stevenson, New England Patriots

Sleeper: MarShawn Lloyd, Green Bay Packers

The Green Bay Packers will be without starting running back Josh Jacobs for the near future. Last year's RB13 has been placed on the commissioner's exempt list following a May arrest for misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property.

With Jacobs out, MarShawn Lloyd is expected to lead Green Bay's backfield. He may lose some touches to Chris Brooks and recent trade acquisition Kaleb Johnson, but he should easily outperform his 174 ADP.

Michael Pittman Jr., Pittsburgh Steelers

Sleeper: Denzel Boston, Cleveland Browns

In recent years, the Cleveland Browns and the term "star fantasy receiver" haven't belonged anywhere near one another. Because of a new offense and some serious questions at quarterback, Cleveland probably won't have a star fantasy wideout in 2026 either.

However, rookie second-round pick Denzel Boston could be a sneaky-good sleeper. His 6'4" frame and tremendous possession skill could make him the Browns' go-to target right away.

Whether Deshaun Watson and/or Shedeur Sanders can get Boston the ball with any consistency remains to be seen. He should be enough of a high-volume target, though, to outpace his 177 ADP.

Chigoziem Okonkwo, Washington Commanders

The Houston Texans are expected to have an improved running game following the addition of David Montgomery. However, they still lack depth behind No. 1 receiver Nico Collins, which could funnel a lot of balls back to tight end Dalton Schultz.

With an ADP of 141, Schultz is largely an afterthought on draft day. However, he's coming off an 82-catch season and finished last year as TE10. Schultz is available late and should be a target for any manager looking to stream at tight end.

*Fantasy scoring and ADP from FantasyPros .
