articles.body: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell has agreed on a four-year contract extension that runs through the 2030 league season, ending on March 31, 2031. The NFL’s Compensation Committee notified the full ownership of the agreement on Sunday. In a memo sent to owners that was obtained by The Associated Press, New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft said: “We believe we are very fortunate to have Roger at the helm for the next four years.” Kraft is the chairman of the league’s compensation committee. “Throughout the negotiation process, the Committee worked closely with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure a deal that aligns Roger’s compensation with the League’s long-term interests and success,” Kraft said. “To that end, the agreement is heavily performance based, with more than 95% of the total compensation tied to Roger’s and the NFL’s performance measured against various metrics and at the discretion of the Compensation Committee.” Financial terms of Goodell’s new contract weren’t immediately known. He reportedly earned $63.9 million for the 2019-20 and 2020-21 seasons. The NFL hasn’t been required to disclose Goodell’s compensation on an annual basis because the league office is no longer structured as a tax-exempt trade association. This is the fifth contract extension for the 67-year-old Goodell, who has served as commissioner since succeeding Paul Tagliabue in 2006. He began his NFL career as an administrative intern in 1982 under then-Commissioner Pete Rozelle. Under Goodell’s leadership, the NFL’s popularity and revenue have skyrocketed. The Washington Commanders were sold for $6.05 billion in 2023 and the Seattle Seahawks were sold for $9.612 billion this offseason, setting a new record. The league has continued expanding its global reach, and is playing a record nine international games this season. The expiration of Goodell’s contract coincides with the end of the current collective bargaining agreement, which also expires in March 2031.

articles.title: Jameis Winston, Giants Agree to Contract Extension as Dart's Backup, Details Revealed in NFL Rumors
articles.summary: Jameis Winston is sticking around the New York Giants for at least a few more seasons.
articles.body:
Jameis Winston is sticking around the New York Giants for at least a few more seasons.

The team reportedly signed the backup quarterback to a two-year, $13 million extension, per NFL reporter Jordan Schultz , who noted that Winston has "become invaluable to the Giants' quarterback room as a leader, a key part of Jaxson Dart's development, and someone the organization views as the best backup quarterback in football."

Winston wasn't the only Giants player to get a new deal on Sunday, however. Guard Jon Runyan agreed to a two-year, $22 million extension with New York, agents Drew Rosenhaus and Kyle Lincoln told ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Buzz: Baker Frustrated with Bucs Talks 😠

Winston, 32, signed a two-year, $8 million contract in March 2025 to join the Giants as a backup quarterback behind Dart and Russell Wilson (Sunday's extension will keep him under contract through the 2028 campaign).

He ultimately appeared in three games (two starts), throwing for 567 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while completing just 56.1 percent of his passes. He also rushed for 23 yards and a score, though the Giants lost both of his starts.

But Winston's impact in the quarterbacks' room and film sessions was important in the development of Dart, who praised him last season.

"He's like a coach on the field, in the film room when we spend extra time," he told reporters in November. "He's quizzing me constantly. He's teaching me things that he's gone through in his past. Our relationship goes far beyond just the football field in the personal life. Handling things that you do good, things that you need to improve on. ... For the team, he brings so much energy and optimism and positivity every single day. He's a guy that never wavers regardless of what's going on around him. It's been a blessing to have him in my corner, for sure."

If everything goes to plan, Winston won't see the field behind the promising Dart beyond garbage time. But the Giants clearly value him as a contingency plan and for what he brings to the table behind the scenes.

articles.title: Rams Star Jokes Teams 'Hate Us' Like 'the New Dodgers' After Aaron Donald, Myles Garrett Additions
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams made the biggest move of the offseason when they traded for reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams made the biggest move of the offseason when they traded for reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett.

Last week, they got even better when Aaron Donald returned to the team after two years retired.

Safety Quentin Lake compared the new-look Rams to another Los Angeles-based sports team that has spent the past few years stacking talent.

"You know all these other teams probably hate us," Rams safety Quentin Lake said, per the Los Angeles Times' Gary Klein . "They think we're like the new Dodgers or something like that."

Lake's assumption that the rest of the NFL hates the Rams might not be too far off. One NFL GM told NFL insider Jordan Schultz that Donald signing with Los Angeles "is so f--ked," so opponents clearly aren't too thrilled with the team.

The Dodgers have won back-to-back World Series, and it wouldn't be a surprise to see them win a third this year. As for the Rams, the success of their super team remains to be seen.

articles.title: Pair of NFL.com experts pick Lions to capture Super Bowl LXI title
articles.summary: As game week arrives, two NFL.com experts picked the Detroit Lions as their preseason pick to win Super Bowl LXI.
articles.body:
As the Lions enter the 2026-27 NFL season, two NFL.com writers picked Detroit to capture its first Super Bowl title in their preseason Super Bowl LXI matchup and champion predictions .

Here are the projected matchups from both writers who believe the Lions will capture the Lombardi Trophy this coming February:

"Just days after winning Comeback Player of the Year, Patrick Mahomes leads comeback K.C. to a Super Bowl performance for the ages. Unfortunately for the Chiefs , Jared Goff wins this duel, 54-51, like it's 2018, and this pride of Lions makes history. Buoyed by a high-octane offense keyed by Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown delighting his homecoming crowd, Detroit will win the franchise's first-ever Super Bowl at the expense of the Chiefs, whose sensational turnaround ends valiantly but with Travis Kelce and Andy Reid retiring just short of another ring."

"After dispatching their former QB Matthew Stafford and the offseason champion Rams in the NFC title game, the Lions give forlorn fans everywhere a reason to believe by beating the Bolts in a battle of Lombardi-less clubs."

Eight NFL.com writers picked the Los Angeles Rams to capture the Lombardi Trophy. Three picked the Buffalo Bills to capture their first Super Bowl championship. Like the Lions, two picked the Cincinnati Bengals and the Houston Texans to capture the crown.

One writer picked the Dallas Cowboys and another picked the Philadelphia Eagles to win the Super Bowl.

The Lions open their regular-season slate on Sunday, Sept. 13 at Ford Field against the New Orleans Saints . Kickoff is at 1 p.m. ET and with the game broadcast on Fox.
